content.text: In Java, the File class from the java.io package provides functionality for file management. You can use it to modify file properties, access file paths and sizes, rename or delete files, list directory contents, and more.

delete(): Deletes the file or directory.
list(): Returns an array of filenames in the directory.
listFiles(): Returns an array of File objects in the directory.
mkdir(): Creates a new directory.
mkdirs(): Creates a new directory, including any non-existing parent directories.
renameTo(File dest): Renames the file to the specified destination.

content.text: Serialization in Java refers to converting an object into a byte stream, and deserialization is the reverse process, where a byte stream is converted back into an object.
To serialize an object, the class must implement the Serializable interface. The ObjectOutputStream class is used to serialize objects into a file.
To deserialize an object, use the ObjectInputStream class, which reads an object from a file.
If a class structure changes (e.g., adding a new field), deserialization may fail due to version mismatch. To handle this, you can specify a unique serialVersionUID.

items: If a class implements Serializable, its subclasses also become serializable.
If a serializable class has a reference to another class, that class must also implement Serializable.
Static members are not serialized, as they belong to the class, not the object.
Elements in arrays/collections must be serializable.
Non-Serializable Objects: If an object is not serializable, it must be marked as transient, or a new serializable class should be defined for it.
InvalidClassException: If the serialVersionUID is not consistent between the serialized class and its updated version, an exception will be thrown during deserialization.
